STATEMENT OF COMPLAINANT
------------------------------------------------------------------------

The complainant, Rohit D'Souza, owner of a bar and restaurant at
Hill Road Bandra West, states that on 14/06/2026 at approximately
21:30 hrs, two persons arrived at his establishment in vehicle no.
MH-04-EF-6602 driven by one Arun Tawde who waited outside.

The first accused Raju Bhai, and the second accused Imran Sheikh,
entered the establishment after closing hours and in the presence of
two staff members threatened the complainant that unless a monthly
sum of Rs. 50,000 was paid commencing immediately, the establishment
would be set on fire and the complainant and his family members would
face grave consequences.

The complainant states that this is the second such visit, the first
having occurred approximately one month prior, around mid-May 2026,
on which occasion a verbal warning only was delivered by the same
first accused accompanied by a different associate whose identity is
not yet established. During that first visit, the complainant was
contacted by the accused on phone number +91-90000-66677 approximately
two hours prior, purportedly to verify the complainant's presence at
the establishment.

Staff members present on 14/06/2026, namely Santosh Kale S/o Bhikaji
Kale R/o Dharavi, and Rekha Pawar W/o Dilip Pawar R/o Mahim, have
given corroborating statements. Both witnesses identified the vehicle
and described the accused.

CIRCUMSTANCES
------------------------------------------------------------------------

On the basis of specific information received on 03/08/2026 regarding
movement of contraband near the Malad West Link Road area, Inspector
Firoz Khan MH-PI-7743 led a raiding party comprising Sub-Inspector
Rekha Nair MH-PSI-9921 and Head Constable Dinesh More MH-HC-1145.

The accused Imran Sheikh and Salim Qureshi were intercepted at
approximately 20:00 hrs near Evershine Nagar, Malad West, arriving
on motorcycle no. MH-07-KL-3305. Upon search in the presence of
independent panchas, a total of 480 grams of a white powdery substance
suspected to be a manufactured narcotic drug was recovered from a
concealed carrier bag in possession of the accused Salim Qureshi.

The second accused Imran Sheikh was found in possession of a mobile
phone with call records showing repeated communication with Salim
Qureshi over the preceding fortnight. The mobile phone bearing number
+91-90000-33344, registered in the name of Imran Sheikh, is seized
as material evidence.

The recovered substance has been sent to the Government Chemical
Analyser for examination and confirmation. Both accused have been
placed under arrest under the provisions of the NDPS Act.

Subsequent inquiries reveal that the accused Imran Sheikh has been
previously named in FIR No. 0112/2026 at Andheri Police Station
(Sections 384 and 506 IPC) and FIR No. 0245/2026 at Dadar Police
Station (Sections 420 and 120B IPC). Crime Branch has been informed
and a request for consolidated investigation is under consideration.

Salim Qureshi has no prior criminal record on file at this station.
His antecedents and associates are being verified.

STATEMENT OF COMPLAINANT
------------------------------------------------------------------------

The complainant, Hasmukh Mehta, a wholesale cloth merchant operating
from Dadar TT Circle, states that in the first week of April 2026, two
persons visited his shop and represented themselves as procurement agents
of a fictional shipping and logistics firm named Global Freight Services.

The first of these persons introduced himself as Imran, the second
as Rajan. They stated that their firm required a large bulk consignment
of cotton fabrics and requested samples and a proforma invoice. On their
second visit on 02/05/2026, all three accused arrived together in
vehicle no. MH-01-DT-1123. The third person, subsequently identified
as Vikram Naik, presented himself as the logistics coordinator.

The accused produced fictitious letterheads and documentation purporting
to be from Global Freight Services and persuaded the complainant to
transfer an advance payment of Rs. 3,50,000 via NEFT to a bank account
they represented as belonging to the firm. The consignment was never
delivered and the accused became unreachable thereafter.

Inquiries with the Registrar of Companies reveal no entity named
Global Freight Services registered at the address provided on the
letterhead. The bank account to which the transfer was made is stated
by the complainant's banker to have been opened in the name of
RK Enterprises, details of which are under investigation.

R/o Nagpada, Mumbai - 400008, Phone: +91-90000-66677, who was present
during the accused's visits, has provided a statement corroborating
the complainant's account and confirming the identities of the accused
from photographs shown to her.

the three accused, with coordinated roles observed across this FIR and
FIR Nos. 0112/2026 (Andheri PS) and 0187/2026 (Kurla PS).

Acting on a tip-off received at approximately 01:30 hrs on 09/07/2026,
